messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring pattern across last 3 incidents: auth provider token throttling -> model-registry auth failures -> cross-region failover not kicking in cleanly. Filling in owners and short actions so we can close outstanding items.
Liam: ack. can you call out the specific failure points?
Maya: TL;DR: (1) token renewals to model-registry are hitting 429s during auth provider maintenance windows, (2) our model-registry client treats 401/429 the same and retries slowly, (3) failover policy favors the same region because cache+sticky-routing persists for 5m.
Arjun: +1. I saw retry storm logs — client backoff not jittered.
Tess: rough impact: several requests stalled, SLO blips for 90s, downstream request queues backed up.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident note added: INC-2025-07-18-298. Reminder set for owners in 48h.
Maya: Proposed owners + quick timelines:
- Model-registry client: Arjun -> add jittered exponential backoff and distinct handling for 429 vs 401 (ETA: PR in 3 business days)
- Auth provider mitigation: Liam -> confirm token rotation windows and request scheduled maintenance SLA with provider, also add local token caching fallback (ETA: negotiation + config changes in 2 weeks)
- Failover behavior: Tess -> reduce sticky routing TTL to 30s for model workloads and add explicit region fallback policy (ETA: config rollout in 1 week)
Liam: sounds good. For auth-provider: I'll open a support case and ask for an elevated SLA and maintenance windows. also will prototype local token cache with grace TTL = 60s.
Arjun: I'll push a small client patch with jitter and split-status handling. example backoff snippet I'll use:```
// pseudo
backoff = base * 2^attempt + random(0, base)
if status == 429 {
  backoff *= 2 // more conservative
}
```
Tess: For failover, a couple of notes: reduce sticky TTL -> we need to ensure cache warmup doesn't regress latency. I'll add 10% traffic canary for TTL change.
Maya: Action items summarized (for tracking):
- A1: Arjun -> client retry PR + unit tests (owner: Arjun, due: 3 business days)
- A2: Liam -> support case + local token cache prototype (owner: Liam, due: 2 weeks)
- A3: Tess -> routing TTL change + canary plan (owner: Tess, due: 1 week)
- A4: Maya -> update postmortem with owners/ETAs and add to recurring incident dashboard (owner: Maya, due: EOD tomorrow)
Liam: adding one more: A5: infra -> add synthetic test that simulates 429s from auth provider so we catch regressions (I'll coordinate with infra).
Maya: Good — please add these to the postmortem doc. I can create follow-up tickets if you prefer.
Arjun: I'll drop a PR link once tests pass.
Tess: Can we have a 15m sync in 48h to confirm progress?
Maya: Yes. @deploy-bot can you schedule a meeting for 48h?
deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Auth Resilience Check-in" — Tue Jul 22 10:00am PT. Invite sent to Maya, Liam, Arjun, Tess.
sre-oncall-bot: Reminder: A1 due in 3 business days.
Liam: FYI — opened support case #SR-54231 and asked for incident timeline and planned maintenance windows.
Maya: Thanks. I'll update the dashboard with the three-incident trend and tag it in the postmortem doc. PTAL after I add owners. :thumbsup:
Tess: thanks all — keeping this in the follow-up lane. minimal churn in thread please, use the postmortem doc for details.
Arjun: noted, will comment on doc when PR is ready.
Liam: closing loop — I'll post SLA response in the doc when provider replies.
Maya: closing here for now. We'll reconvene at the 48h check-in.
